platform.caption: Proposed logical architecture · select a component to inspect its role and research basis.
platform.finding: NIST frames assurance across the lifecycle. OWASP and OSFI identify agent identity, tool authority and traceability as control concerns; Meta separates generation from validation.
platform.decision: Separate context, generation, policy enforcement, independent evaluation and release authority. Preserve a shared evidence record across those boundaries.
platform.words: Engineers and delivery systems supply tasks and approved context. The runtime proposes actions through a policy gateway. Independent sandbox checks and application evaluations supply evidence to the release authority. Traces and decisions feed the evidence store; curated failures become regression cases.

strategic-system.caption: Strategic target state · analyst outlook informs the ambition; the capability design is our synthesis.
strategic-system.finding: Gartner forecasts broader AI assistant use. McKinsey’s survey connects reported impact with changes across delivery and the operating model. DORA describes AI as an amplifier of the surrounding system.
strategic-system.decision: Invest in shared evaluation assets, platform controls and operational learning that serve both AI-assisted engineering and AI products. These sources do not establish a bank-specific return.
strategic-system.words: AI for QE and QE for AI share testable intent, independent assurance and operational learning. That common capability supports validated delivery, trustworthy AI behavior and reuse across teams.

testgen-evidence.caption: Observed industrial evaluation · Meta TestGen-LLM, FSE 2024, §3.3. The three bars use the same test-class denominator.
testgen-evidence.finding: In Meta’s 86-component Kotlin evaluation, 75% of target test classes gained at least one generated test that built; 57% had one that also passed reliably; 25% had one that also increased line coverage.
testgen-evidence.decision: Treat generation as a candidate factory. Require independent checks for stability and added test value; use fault detection where possible because coverage alone does not establish semantic quality.
testgen-evidence.words: The bars have a common zero-to-100-percent axis. The qualifying share drops from 75% for build success to 57% for reliable passing and 25% for added coverage. These percentages describe test classes, not individual generated tests.

evaluation-system.caption: Proposed evaluation and release architecture · the unit of assurance is the configured application.
evaluation-system.finding: NIST treats evaluation and risk management as lifecycle activities. Evaluation product documentation supports versioned datasets and comparisons; judge calibration still requires local evidence.
evaluation-system.decision: Compare baseline and candidate configurations against held-out cases, gate releases on agreed floors, then turn reviewed production failures into regression cases.
evaluation-system.words: Versioned application configurations and a held-out evaluation corpus feed comparable runs and independent scoring. A failed release gate holds the change for investigation. A passing gate leads to controlled deployment and production monitoring; curated failures refresh the corpus.

test-sequence.caption: Illustrative payment-API workflow · the approved contract defines correct behavior; all execution stays within the sandbox.
test-sequence.finding: Meta’s generation work filters candidates through executable checks; mutation-guided testing tests whether a candidate detects a fault. Agent guidance requires authority to be bounded at the action boundary.
test-sequence.decision: Generate a negative-amount test from an approved contract, execute it through a scoped gateway, retain the independent fault-detection result and route the evidence to a human reviewer.
test-sequence.words: The engineer supplies the contract. The agent requests scoped context and proposes a test. The gateway authorizes sandbox execution. CI checks the candidate against a seeded boundary fault. The reviewer receives assertions and test evidence before using existing merge controls.

research-decisions.caption: Research → proposed design → evidence to retain. The architecture choices are our synthesis, not publisher endorsements.
research-decisions.finding: The sources address different failure modes: verification effort, weak generated tests, lifecycle change and the consequences of agent actions.
research-decisions.decision: Translate each finding into an observable design requirement. Review burden needs effort telemetry; test generation needs a quality gate; changing AI needs repeatable evaluation; tool use needs enforceable permissions.
research-decisions.words: DORA informs joined effort measurement. Meta informs independent test-quality gates. NIST informs versioned evaluation and feedback. OWASP and OSFI inform external permission enforcement. Each design response has an associated evidence record.

capability-horizons.caption: Proposed capability horizons · progression depends on demonstrated outcomes and authority, rather than calendar dates.
capability-horizons.finding: Industry research places AI adoption within delivery-system and operating-model change. Assurance guidance makes the consequences of actions and ongoing monitoring relevant to expansion.
capability-horizons.decision: Develop bounded assistance first, connect shared assurance services next and expand agent authority only after local quality, repeatability and recovery evidence supports it.
capability-horizons.words: Horizon one is trusted assistance, gated by local quality and net effort. Horizon two is connected assurance, gated by repeatability across teams. Horizon three is controlled agents, gated by safe actions and tested resilience.

evidence-contrasts.caption: Two randomized-study findings · different outcomes and settings; neither percentage is a QE savings benchmark.
evidence-contrasts.finding: Cui et al. report a 26.08% increase in completed tasks across three field experiments. METR’s early-2025 trial reports a 19% increase in completion time for experienced developers on familiar repositories.
evidence-contrasts.decision: Segment pilots by task and user population, retain verification effort, and measure quality alongside throughput. METR’s later follow-up has selection concerns; it does not supply a clean causal time trend.
evidence-contrasts.words: Cui: 4,867 developers, completed tasks +26.08%, standard error 10.3 percentage points. METR: 16 developers, 246 tasks, completion time +19%, 95% confidence interval +2% to +39%. The studies measure distinct outcomes and should not be pooled.

threat-boundary.caption: Proposed threat model · the highlighted test follows an injected request all the way to enforcement and recovery.
threat-boundary.finding: OWASP identifies risks arising from untrusted inputs and agent tool use. OSFI’s July 2026 bulletin discusses agent identity, scoped tool access, traceability and resilience as sound practices.
threat-boundary.decision: Test the system’s response when poisoned context asks for an unauthorized action. Assert no side effect, a recorded denial and a bounded escalation path—not just a polite refusal in the model’s answer.
threat-boundary.words: Untrusted documents, code, tool output and memory reach the agent runtime. The agent can request an action, but the gateway checks identity, resource and policy. Permitted calls reach scoped tools. Denied calls cause no side effect and stop or escalate.

evidence-model.caption: Proposed measurement schema · identifiers link work, execution, review and observed outcomes.
evidence-model.finding: DORA’s qualitative work highlights verification friction. Experimental findings depend on the task and population; reported AI impact is not a universal savings rate.
evidence-model.decision: Compare like tasks and account for preparation, execution, review, correction and rework. Link quality and cost to the same cohort; recognize monetary value only with a confirmed capture mechanism.
evidence-model.words: A task has multiple runs; a run may have several review records. Outcomes link through task and artifact identifiers. A cohort comparison joins baseline effort, run and review effort, rework and defects. Version identifiers make changes in tool configuration auditable.

opportunity-map.caption: Proposed portfolio screen · qualitative categories, not a scored market ranking.
opportunity-map.finding: Industrial cases demonstrate bounded test generation and diagnosis. Agent guidance adds the consequences of actions to the evaluation problem.
opportunity-map.decision: Select an initial workflow with an independent check and limited authority; assess judgment-heavy and consequential workflows separately.
opportunity-map.words: A two-by-two screen separates easy-to-verify results from expert judgment, and advice from greater action authority. Test drafts and log-linked diagnosis are candidate starting points.

ownership-system.caption: Proposed ownership model · adapt to existing institutional accountability.
ownership-system.finding: DORA and McKinsey place AI adoption in the surrounding delivery organization. NIST frames governance across the lifecycle.
ownership-system.decision: Assign a product owner for outcomes, a platform owner for services and a separate challenge function; include operations and value capture.
ownership-system.words: Product and QE accountability flows to the delivery team. Shared platform services enable delivery; delivery and risk owners challenge its evidence. Operations and value owners use the resulting outcomes.

investment-stack.caption: Proposed investment architecture · layer size does not represent budget allocation.
investment-stack.finding: Organizational research emphasizes delivery foundations. Evaluation tools expose datasets and run comparisons, but task fit still requires local validation.
investment-stack.decision: Fund reusable services centrally while product teams own domain-specific quality assets. Use adapters and evidence export requirements to support substitution.
investment-stack.words: Three example domains contribute different quality assets. They use a common assurance layer, which connects through replaceable model and tool adapters.

strategic-scorecard.caption: Proposed leadership scorecard · measures and decisions, with no invented performance values.
strategic-scorecard.finding: Studies use different tasks, populations and outcome measures; verification effort can offset generation gains.
strategic-scorecard.decision: Tie each strategic objective to observable evidence and an explicit decision. Keep quality and control floors alongside capacity measures.
strategic-scorecard.words: Four rows connect delivery capacity, trustworthy outcomes, reusable capability and controlled autonomy to evidence and leadership decisions.

governance-loop.caption: Proposed governance loop · assess applicability through existing risk functions.
governance-loop.finding: NIST links governance to lifecycle risk management. OSFI discusses AI accountability and resilience; revised E-23 has a future effective date.
governance-loop.decision: Maintain an inventory and an explicit authority boundary, then revisit them after incidents or material changes. This diagram is not a compliance certification.
governance-loop.words: Inventory informs authority limits. Evidence review supports an approved scope. Operations feed incidents and service changes back into the inventory and authority decision.

context-route.caption: Proposed context architecture · retrieval improves task evidence; permissions remain separately enforced.
context-route.finding: Lifecycle guidance covers input provenance; agent risk guidance addresses untrusted context and access scope.
context-route.decision: Filter retrieval using current authorization, retain a versioned input snapshot and test grounding separately from action permissions.
context-route.words: Approved sources feed scoped retrieval and a minimal context snapshot. The runtime treats that content as evidence. Retrieval checks evaluate relevance and access; the action gateway retains authority.

configuration-bundle.caption: Proposed release manifest · the model name alone cannot identify the evaluated system.
configuration-bundle.finding: Lifecycle assurance requires tracking changing system components. Evaluation platforms compare configurations and datasets.
configuration-bundle.decision: Bind the code, prompt, retrieval, tool policy and evaluator versions to one release identity; keep the run and decision references with it.
configuration-bundle.words: A manifest contains model and prompt, retrieval and data, tools and memory, and the evaluation contract. A release identity binds those versions to evaluated runs and approval.

test-oracle.caption: Illustrative payment contract · expected behavior is proposed for this example.
test-oracle.finding: Meta separates generated tests from executable validation and extends test value beyond code coverage through fault-oriented testing.
test-oracle.decision: Review assertions against an approved behavior contract and evaluate side effects. Use relevant faults to challenge a test that merely matches current behavior.
test-oracle.words: The approved contract and implementation inform a candidate test. Separate oracle review checks intended behavior; independent execution checks both valid code and a seeded fault.

mutation-loop.caption: Design pattern informed by Meta ACH · detecting selected mutants does not prove all real faults are covered.
mutation-loop.finding: Meta ACH uses modeled faults to drive test generation and checks generated tests against original and mutated code.
mutation-loop.decision: Retain both execution results and review mutation relevance. A test gains useful evidence when it distinguishes intended behavior from a meaningful fault.
mutation-loop.words: A fault concern drives a candidate test. It must pass original code and fail a relevant mutated version. Combined evidence reaches review; weak results lead to refining the concern.

diagnosis-workflow.caption: Google case study (2026) plus a proposed local workflow · populations remain separate.
diagnosis-workflow.finding: Google reports 90.14% root-cause accuracy on 71 reviewed failures and deployment across 52,635 distinct failing tests.
diagnosis-workflow.decision: Attach relevant log evidence to a diagnosis, retain reviewer corrections and measure local accuracy separately from reach.
diagnosis-workflow.words: A failing test feeds an assistant and then an engineer review. The outcome record captures corrections and effort. Separate panels show the small accuracy sample and larger deployment population.

flaky-repair.caption: Proposed repair assurance loop · inspired by a six-month industrial Go case.
flaky-repair.finding: FlakyGuard combines targeted execution context with LLM-based repair. Its paper discusses the risk of fixes that weaken test semantics.
flaky-repair.decision: Require reproducibility, preserved assertions and independent repeated validation before proposing a merge.
flaky-repair.words: The workflow reproduces a flaky failure, gathers targeted context, proposes a repair and validates it. Semantically weak or unstable repairs return to diagnosis.

corpus-design.caption: Proposed corpus design · set sizes depend on the task and consequences of failure.
corpus-design.finding: NIST emphasizes representative evaluation. Evaluation tooling supports curated datasets and feedback from operational traces.
corpus-design.decision: Separate tuning from release evaluation, group related examples during splitting and preserve adversarial scenarios with explicit expected behavior.
corpus-design.words: Candidate cases pass through privacy review, deduplication and labeling. They feed development, held-out and adversarial sets with distinct uses.

gateway-sequence.caption: Proposed denial sequence · the test verifies execution and evidence, beyond the model’s response.
gateway-sequence.finding: Agent risk guidance identifies tool misuse and identity problems. OSFI discusses scoped identities, tool restrictions and activity logs.
gateway-sequence.decision: Check policy at the gateway before invocation. A denial must produce no tool side effect and a traceable reason.
gateway-sequence.words: The runtime requests a production write. The gateway evaluates scope, records a denial and returns it to the runtime. The scoped tool is never invoked.

execution-isolation.caption: Proposed deployment boundaries · zones represent authority, not a specific cloud product.
execution-isolation.finding: Agent guidance emphasizes scoped tool access and separation of consequential actions. Industrial generation patterns use independent execution checks.
execution-isolation.decision: Keep workers without production credentials, isolate test execution and allow only reviewed artifacts through existing release controls.
execution-isolation.words: An orchestration worker invokes an ephemeral sandbox. Controlled artifacts reach review, then protected release systems. Production authority never belongs to the generating worker.

release-gate.caption: Proposed release logic · no universal score threshold is asserted.
release-gate.finding: Lifecycle assurance considers system-specific risks and uncertainty. Evaluation tools support run and case-level comparisons.
release-gate.decision: Use mandatory floors for critical behaviors, then inspect the distribution of changes before authorizing rollout.
release-gate.words: Comparable runs reach a mandatory-floor check. Failure holds the candidate. Passing candidates proceed to review of scenario-level regressions and remaining uncertainty.

fallback-state.caption: Proposed recovery state machine · triggers and fallback capacity require local exercises.
fallback-state.finding: Lifecycle and agent guidance make recovery relevant to assurance. OSFI discusses tested AI failure scenarios and continuity measures.
fallback-state.decision: Separate containment, fallback and authorized resumption; explicitly handle actions that cannot be reversed by a model rollback.
fallback-state.words: A trigger moves normal operation to containment and fallback. Recovery review verifies a fix before an owner authorizes resumption. Completed side effects require separate reconciliation.

trace-pipeline.caption: Proposed event architecture · traces and derived evidence need their own data controls.
trace-pipeline.finding: Evaluation workflows use operational feedback, while agent risk guidance calls attention to tool and action behavior.
trace-pipeline.decision: Join application events, gateway decisions and reviewer corrections without broadly copying sensitive raw prompts into monitoring systems.
trace-pipeline.words: Three event streams enter a controlled telemetry boundary. The joined records support operations, platform monitoring and reviewed regression-case curation.

strategy-choices.caption: Authored strategic choices · no bank maturity or savings claim.
strategy-choices.finding: Industry outlook and lifecycle guidance support broader AI participation and independent assurance.
strategy-choices.decision: Use shared assurance as the strategic center; delegate actions only as boundaries and evidence mature.
strategy-choices.words: Local assistants accelerate individual tasks. Shared assurance makes expectations, evaluation and evidence reusable. Bounded agents add delegated actions and stronger recovery obligations. These are design choices, not measured maturity scores.

bank-workflow.caption: Illustrative financial-services workflow · current-state row is a hypothesis, not an observed bank condition.
bank-workflow.finding: Test-generation studies use quality gates; verification work remains part of the workflow.
bank-workflow.decision: Join a domain-owned payment contract to shared evidence services and existing release authority.
bank-workflow.words: The current-state hypothesis has local interpretation, test writing, review and late evidence assembly. The target versions the approved payment rule, generates tests in a scoped sandbox, independently checks fault detection and retains the reviewer decision and release evidence.

contract-chain.caption: Runnable reference contracts · synthetic example, not a production integration.
contract-chain.finding: Lifecycle and action-risk guidance require versioned evidence and scoped authority.
contract-chain.decision: Provide joined artifacts and negative fixtures so the logical design can be exercised.
contract-chain.words: A payment test task binds permitted context, resource scope and deadline. A policy decision authorizes only the sandbox action. An evaluation manifest joins artifact and corpus versions. The evidence record links task, policy and evaluation and remains held for human review.

failure-resolution.caption: Proposed QA workflow · a temporary quarantine is not a successful repair.
failure-resolution.finding: AutoDiagnose informs evidence-based failure triage. FlakyGuard reports reproducibility and accepted repairs using separate denominators.
failure-resolution.decision: Verify repairs against the original failure. Require an owner, expiry and replacement coverage for a confirmed flaky test placed in quarantine.
failure-resolution.words: Capture CI traces, fixture versions and repeatability evidence. An owner confirms whether the cause is product, test, data or environment. Proposed repairs require an independent retest and relevant regression. A confirmed flaky test may instead enter a time-limited quarantine with replacement coverage. Both paths keep a resolution record; the quarantined test remains open until restored.
